A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same sMDM research work. All 13 pages in each version, including the three-page supplementary material, are readable and support comparison of text, equations, figures, and tables.

before.justification: v1 reports original motion-generation experiments, component ablations, and architecture comparisons on HumanML3D, including supplementary motion-in-betweening results in Table 7.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical results in Tables 1–7 and the qualitative motion-generation examples.

M1.justification: The sparse-keyframe masking, feature interpolation, Lipschitz components, keyframe selection, and dynamic mask updates are unchanged. The downstream adaptations and supplementary implementation descriptions also match.

E1.justification: Both versions retain the same HumanML3D evaluations covering text-to-motion generation, long-sequence generation, character control, and motion in-betweening. No dataset or test scenario is added or removed.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is identical within Tables 1–7 and the qualitative comparisons. This includes the text-to-motion baselines, PriorMDM, DiP/DiP-T, and the supplementary MotionDiffuse and CondMDI comparisons.

E3.justification: Evaluation metrics, model configurations, diffusion-step settings, keyframe reduction rates, and testing procedures are unchanged. Appendix C.2 retains the same motion-in-betweening evaluation with five conditioning keyframes.

E4.justification: Both retain the component ablations in Table 1, dynamic-mask analysis in Table 2, reduction-rate comparisons in Table 4, and architecture analyses in Appendix C, including the unsuccessful U-Net adaptation.

E5.justification: Statistical reporting is unchanged. Neither version supplies repeated-run or seed counts, confidence intervals, or significance tests; the tables retain the same point-estimate reporting.

E6.justification: All numerical entries and qualitative results match. For example, sMDM's Table 1 FID remains 0.130, and sCondMDI's supplementary Table 7 FID remains 0.551. No results or rankings are added, removed, or revised.

T1.justification: Equations (1)–(9), including the diffusion formulation, Lipschitz regularization, keyframe-area definition, and imputation equation, are unchanged. No mathematical assumptions, derivations, or proofs are added or revised.

C1.justification: The scientific claims about sparse-keyframe diffusion, improved text alignment and motion quality, performance with fewer diffusion steps, and downstream applicability remain unchanged in the abstract, introduction, and conclusion.

C2.justification: Both retain the interpretation linking more dynamic motions to poorer transition-distribution scores in Section 5.2, the Transformer-focused applicability qualification in the conclusion, and the explanation of the U-Net adaptation's failure in Appendix C.2.

D1.justification: v1's abstract states that source code and pretrained models will be released upon acceptance; v2 deletes this statement without replacement access information. Implementation details in Appendices A–B remain unchanged. This is a change in release disclosure, not evidence that available resources were withdrawn.

R1.justification: The cited works and research positioning are unchanged. References 12 and 25 only update their citation-page back-references from page 3 to page 2 because the surrounding text reflows.

P1.justification: v2 removes one sentence from the abstract and updates the arXiv version/date marking. The remaining prose, terminology, section organization, and supplementary narrative are unchanged.

P2.justification: The shortened abstract causes limited text reflow across columns and pages 1–3. Figures 1–4 and Tables 1–7 retain their content, captions, and designs; the supplementary layout is unchanged.

improvement.justification: The scientific argument, empirical evidence, limitations, and supplementary technical content are unchanged. Deleting the conditional code/model release promise reduces release-policy information but removes neither an existing access link nor implementation instructions. Together with the minor text reflow, this does not materially change the paper's overall quality.
